t: Disappearance Of A Left Wing Writer Named Liu Kien-Nan

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. R. S. D. REGI T [G]
File No.
No. D
S., Special Branch photokd
Date November 24, 1933.

Subject (in full) Disappearance of a Left Wing writer named Liu Kien-nan (樓建南).

Made by D.I.Kuh Hao-hwa Forwarded by D.I. [Signature]

With reference to the endorse of the officer i/c
Special Branch on the attached newspaper translation regarding
a "Left Wing" writer named Liu Kien-nan (樓建南) alias Liu Suh-yie
(樓適夷) alias Tseng I-Yien (張一樂) who is stated to have been
missing since September 1933, I have to report the following:-

According to discreet enquiries made by the undersigned
assisted by D.S. Umonoto, it has been ascertained that the
individual in question was arrested by Chapei Constable No.2764,
at the instance of two unknown officers of the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau, at the Uchiyama Book Store, No.1001 North Szechuen
Road, while he was making some purchases in that shop at about
7 p.m. September 17, 1933. According to a shop witness the
two Public Safety Bureau officers remained outside the shop on
N. Szechuen Road while the Chapei constable effected Liu's arrest
inside the bookstore.

Mr. Hasegawa, manager of the Uchiyama Book Shop,
later made a report on the occurrence to the local Japanese
Consulate.

It has been secretly ascertained that Liu Kien-nan
was subsequently escorted to Nanking where he expressed
sentiments of repentance. Up to the present, however, he
has not been released.

Kuh Hao-hwa
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

日期 1933年11月24日。

主题（全称） 左翼作家楼建南失踪案。

由督察顾浩华呈报 转呈者 督察 [签名]

兹参照附件中关于一名名为楼建南（Liu Kien-nan）、别名楼适夷（Liu Suh-yie）、别名张一乐（Tseng I-Yien）的“左翼”作家自1933年9月起失踪的报纸译文上特别处主管警官的批注，本人谨报告如下：-

经本人会同副督察乌莫诺托（Umonoto）进行审慎调查，已查明该人于1933年9月17日晚7时许，在四川北路1001号内山书店购物时，应上海公安局两名不明身份警官的要求，被闸北巡捕第2764号逮捕。据店内目击者称，当时两名公安局警官留在四川北路店外，而由闸北巡捕在书店内实施了对楼的逮捕。

内山书店经理长谷川先生事后就此事向日本驻当地领事馆作了报告。

经秘密查悉，楼建南随后被押解至南京，并在那里表达了悔过之意。然而截至目前，他尚未获释。

顾浩华
督察

特别处主管警官。

November 10, 1933. Morning Translation.

COMMUNISM

"Japanese are behind the scenes in the activities of the Red bandits. The military attache Morioka at Hankow and a Japanese named Furukawa at Shanghai are undertaking the work in their respective cities. Furukawa resides on the fourth floor of a certain dispensary on Broadway; he is a law and political student. In all, there are forty Japanese, all from Japan, who have been detailed to bandit regions in Hupeh and Kiangsi to supply them with firearms and funds."
A Peiping telegram published by the Central Daily News reads:-
"At Hankow there are Japanese organizations supplying the Chinese Red bandits in the Upper Yangtsze with firearms. These arms are transported to Hankow in Japanese warships and stored in Japanese houses."
These are the true facts in the conspiracy of the Chinese Red bandits with the Japanese.
The bandits have betrayed the people. When they arrive in a new district, they first carry out the following acts:-
1) Overthrow the district gentry and compel the people to contribute to their treasury.
2) The people are made to comply with all their directions.
3) Labourers and peasants are not to be imposed upon.
The report that officers, soldiers and coolies in the Red districts are treated on an equal basis is all empty talk. In reality, the livelihood of Red soldiers is very distressful, but their leaders enjoy excellent treatment.

Holmes (福尔摩斯), a mosquito paper, dated Nov. 9:

DISAPPEARANCE OF ANOTHER LEFT WING WRITER.

A left wing writer named Liu Kien-nan (楼建南) has been reported missing since September. He is also known under the name of Suh Yie (适夷). He was formerly an editor of the "Jen Nyi Sin Wan" (文艺新闻). He became famous when he wrote a drama entitled "Huo Loo" (活路). His writings were mostly published in the "Pei Ter" (北斗), the Tung Fong (东方), the "Wen Hsueh" (文学) and other magazines.
He was an active member of the Left Wing Writers Alliance and editor of a certain paper related to the Anti-War Congress.
It is being said that Liu has met the same fate as Ting Ling (丁玲) and Pan Sin-nyi (潘梓年), while others believe that he is still alive.
He has a sweetheart named Miss S. She has been to the Hengenbeck Circus to inquire about him as she was labouring under the fear that he might have been devoured by one of the wild beasts.

（左侧手写批注：$2, For comment please MK）

S. I. Kirk
88R - 1/11.

1933年11月10日。晨间译文。

共产主义

“日本人在赤匪活动背后操纵。汉口的武官森冈（Morioka）和上海的日本人古川（Furukawa）正在各自的城市从事这项工作。古川居住在百老汇路某诊所的四楼；他是一名法律和政治系学生。总共有四十名日本人，全部来自日本，已被派往湖北和江西的匪区，向他们提供枪支和资金。”
《中央日报》刊登的一则北平电文称：-
“在汉口，有日本组织向长江上游的中国赤匪提供枪支。这些武器由日本军舰运至汉口，并储存在日本人的房屋内。”
这些是中国赤匪与日本人勾结阴谋的真实事实。
匪徒背叛了人民。当他们到达一个新地区时，首先实施以下行为：-
1) 推翻该地区士绅，强迫人民向其金库捐款。
2) 强迫人民服从其所有指令。
3) 不压迫劳工和农民。
所谓赤区内的军官、士兵和苦力待遇平等的说法纯属空谈。实际上，赤军士兵的生活非常困苦，但其首领却享受优厚待遇。

《福尔摩斯》（Holmes），一份小报，11月9日刊：

又一名左翼作家失踪。

据报道，一名名为楼建南的左翼作家自9月起失踪。他也以适夷（Suh Yie）之名为人所知。他曾任《文艺新闻》（Jen Nyi Sin Wan）编辑。他因创作一部名为《活路》（Huo Loo）的戏剧而闻名。他的作品主要发表在《北斗》（Pei Ter）、《东方》（Tung Fong）、《文学》（Wen Hsueh）等杂志上。
他是左翼作家联盟的活跃成员，也是某份与反战大会有关的报刊的编辑。
有人说楼的遭遇与丁玲（Ting Ling）和潘梓年（Pan Sin-nyi）相同，而另一些人则认为他仍然活着。
他有一位姓S的女友。她曾去亨根贝克马戏团（Hengenbeck Circus）打听他的消息，因为她担心他可能已被猛兽吞食。

（左侧手写批注：$2，请MK评论）

S. I. Kirk
88R - 1/11.
